questions.question_text: For the sequence $6, 11, 16, 21, 26, 31, \dots$, what is the value of the partial sum $S_{4}$?

options.why: Gave the 4th term $a_{4}$ instead of the partial sum $S_{4}$.
Added five terms ($S_{5}$) instead of four terms ($S_{4}$).
Left out the first term $6$: $11+16+21=48$.

questions.question_text:
A sequence is given by $a_{n} = 3n - 1$.
What is the value of the partial sum $S_{3}$?

options.why: Gave the 3rd term $a_{3}$ instead of the sum of the first three terms.
Used $3n$ instead of $3n-1$, giving $3+6+9=18$.
Added four terms including $a_{4} = 11$.
Gave the fourth term instead of adding the first four terms.
Added the fifth term $405$ as well: $200+405=605$.
Left out the first term $5$: $15+45+135=195$.

questions.question_text:
A sequence has $n$th term $a_{n}=n^{2}+3$.
What is $S_{6}-S_{3}$?

options.why: Removed the fourth term as well, calculating $S_{6}-S_{4}=28+39=67$.
Gave $S_{6}=4+7+12+19+28+39$ without subtracting $S_{3}=23$.
Included the third term $12$, calculating $S_{6}-S_{2}=12+19+28+39=98$.

questions.question_text:

What is $S_{4}$?

options.why: Gave the fourth term $2(4)+1=9$ instead of the sum.
Omitted the $+1$ from every term, adding $2+4+6+8=20$.
Included the fifth term $11$, calculating $S_{5}=24+11=35$.

questions.question_text:
A sequence has $n$th term $a_{n}=n^{2}-3$.
What is $S_{7}-S_{3}$?

options.why: Included the third term $6$, adding $6+13+22+33+46=120$.
Removed the fourth term $13$ as well, adding only $22+33+46=101$.

questions.question_text:
A sequence has $n$th term $a_{n}=3n^{2}-n$.
What is $S_{5}-S_{2}$?

options.why: Gave the fifth term $3(5)^{2}-5=70$ instead of adding the required terms.
Removed the third term $24$ as well, adding only $44+70=114$.
Gave $S_{5}=2+10+24+44+70=150$ without subtracting $S_{2}=12$.

questions.question_text:
A sequence has $n$th term $a_{n}=4n^{2}+2n$.
What is $S_{5}-S_{2}$?

options.why: Gave the fifth term $4(5)^{2}+2(5)=110$ instead of adding the required terms.
Removed the third term $42$ as well, adding only $72+110=182$.
Gave $S_{5}=6+20+42+72+110=250$ without subtracting $S_{2}=26$.

questions.question_text:
A sequence has $n$th term $a_{n}=n^{2}-4$.
What is $S_{6}-S_{2}$?

options.why: Removed the third term $5$ as well, adding only $12+21+32=65$.
Added $S_{2}=-3$ instead of subtracting it, calculating $S_{6}+S_{2}=67-3=64$.
Omitted the $-4$ from each of the four required terms, adding $9+16+25+36=86$.
